expert_decision.location: Section 1 (Introduction, line 31); Section 4.1 (RQ1: Replication of Morrison et al.'s Findings, lines 63–72)
expert_decision.quote: Our study is opportunistic. We have a recent data set from an as-yet unpublished study, which enables us to replicate analyses from two earlier publications. We ask: RQ1 Morrison et al. [49] report good discriminant validity and internal reliability for a programming-domain adaptation of Leppink's [33] CL questionnaire, which is based on the threecomponent Old CLT. expert_decision.reason: Simmonds et al. (2021, 10.1145/3430665.3456356) explicitly frame their paper as an empirical replication of two earlier publications using a new dataset of 175 introductory Python programming students: RQ1 replicates Morrison, Dorn, and Guzdial (2014, 'Measuring cognitive load in introductory CS: Adaptation of an instrument', Proceedings of the Tenth Annual Conference on International Computing Education Research, ICER '14, pp. 131–138, ref. [49]), and RQ2 replicates Jiang & Kalyuga (2020, 10.20982/tqmp.16.3.p216, ref. [22]). Section 4.1 ('RQ1: Replication of Morrison et al.'s Findings') re-runs the three-factor CFA, EFA, and Cronbach's alpha reliability analyses on the adapted CS Cognitive Load Component Survey and directly compares the empirical results in Table 1 against Morrison et al. (2014). Only Jiang & Kalyuga (2020) is present in the shipped dataset (input_row_index 2500); Morrison, Dorn, & Guzdial (2014) is a distinct primary empirical study missing from the shipped rows. Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this item.
